newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end mixed on uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end mixed on uncertainty.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed in slow trade on Friday on uncertainties over the short-term market trend, traders said.
The key January 1997 contract ended at 3,100 yuan ($373) per tonne, losing 40 yuan. It opened at 3,100 and stayed at that level for the whole session.
March rose 45 to 3,145, May fell 70 to 3,100, July was up 10 to 3,230, September was unchanged at 3,350 and November increased 15 to 3,365.
Combined volume fell to 10,400 tonnes from 17,300.
Traders said many investors were staying on the sidelines with the approach of the delivery date for the January 1997 contract and the Chinese lunar new year holiday.
"Most investors are not willing to build fresh positions in the short term, resulting in slow trading," one trader said.
"Uncertainties over the short-term market trend also led many investors to offset their positions and take a wait-and-see attitude," he added.
Traders expect soybeans to move around the 3,100-yuan level in the next few days.
